input.summary:
Room "I-house west room" now places no furnace of its own: the chimneys part's hearth_nook already puts the lit east-facing stove at 26,3,12, so the refused write is gone.
The room keeps its barrel, fence/stair settee, table slab and two hanging lanterns, all in air.
./make.sh shows "part room: I-house west room: 7 placed" with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE; build.nbt was produced (7293 cells).

waste.what: Found the clash by reading the refusal and then probing the saved build.nbt for the block already at 26,3,12, then grepping chimneys.mjs to see which part owned that cell. Three steps to answer a question the build could answer directly.
waste.cost: 3 tool calls, one node probe, one grep; one make.sh rerun to confirm
waste.tool: mcd plan build.nbt --rooms rooms.json --only <room> already marks cells another part built as 'o'; a refusal line naming the owning part and the block (e.g. 'furnace at 26,3,12 is from chimneys.mjs hearth_nook; drop it from this part') would have made the fix a single edit

waste.what: Hand-checked that the earlier furnace's facing (east) and lit state match what this room's layout expected, by reading the state from the saved nbt.
waste.tool: runParts report could list each refused write with the existing block's state and facing, so a clash is judged on sight
